long_biography.plain_text:
Engibous earned bachelor's and master's degrees in electrical engineering from Purdue University and joined Texas Instruments as an integrated-circuit design engineer in 1976. He advanced through the semiconductor group, managing linear and application-specific products before becoming its president and then the company's president and chief executive.

As chief executive, Engibous narrowed Texas Instruments from a broad electronics conglomerate toward semiconductors, shedding defense and memory-chip operations while concentrating on digital signal processors and analog chips. He later became chairman, handed the chief executive role to Rich Templeton and retired from Texas Instruments in 2008. He subsequently brought his technology and financial experience to the boards of J. C. Penney and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company.
long_biography.html:
Engibous earned bachelor's and master's degrees in electrical engineering from Purdue University and joined Texas Instruments as an integrated-circuit design engineer in 1976. He advanced through the semiconductor group, managing linear and application-specific products before becoming its president and then the company's president and chief executive.

As chief executive, Engibous narrowed Texas Instruments from a broad electronics conglomerate toward semiconductors, shedding defense and memory-chip operations while concentrating on digital signal processors and analog chips. He later became chairman, handed the chief executive role to Rich Templeton and retired from Texas Instruments in 2008. He subsequently brought his technology and financial experience to the boards of J. C. Penney and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company.
